tasks.purpose: 分析成人在线学习的原因并评价其发展
tasks.setting: Many adults now choose to take short online courses alongside their work rather than attend classes at a college. These courses can be studied from home, and participants often have some choice over when to complete the lessons.
tasks.lead: Why do adults choose these courses? Is this a positive or negative development?
bullets: Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
must: 解释成人选择短期在线课程的原因，评价这一发展，并以理由和相关例证支持两项回答。
tasks.model:
Adults who want to continue learning increasingly have a choice between a college classroom and a short course delivered online. Many choose the latter because it fits around employment and removes the need to travel. Although online study is not suitable for every subject or learner, I consider this development positive overall.

The main attraction is flexibility. People with jobs and family responsibilities cannot always attend a lesson at the same time each week. A recorded lesson can instead be watched in the evening or during a break, and a learner can return to a difficult section. Online courses may also be accessible to people who live far from a college. For example, a worker in a rural area can study bookkeeping from home without arranging a long journey after work.

This wider access is valuable because adults can update skills or explore an interest without leaving their jobs. A short course also allows someone to try a subject before committing to a longer qualification. These benefits are particularly clear when materials are well organised and learners can ask a tutor for feedback. The convenience of access should not, however, be confused with a guarantee that every course is effective.

There are limitations. Practical subjects may require equipment and supervision that cannot be supplied through a screen, while some students need a regular timetable or personal encouragement to finish. Colleges can address part of this difficulty by combining online materials with occasional workshops and providing clear channels for questions. Learners should also be able to check the content and assessment before enrolling.

Overall, adults choose online courses largely because they make learning easier to fit into ordinary life. This is a beneficial change when course providers preserve opportunities for feedback and recognise that some skills still need face-to-face practice.

tasks.purpose: 分析学校使用数字作业平台的原因并评价其发展
tasks.setting: Some secondary schools now use a digital platform to distribute homework and receive completed assignments. Teachers can post instructions in one place, and pupils can submit their work without handing in a paper copy during a lesson.
tasks.lead: Why do schools use these platforms? Is this a positive or negative development?
bullets: Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
must: 解释学校使用数字作业平台的原因，评价这一发展，并以理由和相关例证支持两项回答。
tasks.model:
Digital homework platforms are becoming part of the routine in some secondary schools. Schools adopt them to organise assignments and make submission more convenient. In my view, the change is beneficial if schools ensure that pupils can access the system and still receive meaningful feedback.

One reason for using a platform is that it keeps instructions, deadlines and submitted work together. A pupil who was absent can check what the class was asked to do, while a teacher can see which assignments have arrived without collecting a stack of paper. The system can also make it easier to distribute a corrected instruction to the whole class. These advantages matter when several teachers and classes must keep track of different tasks.

The same organisation can help pupils manage their work. For instance, a student who forgets the details of a science assignment can return to the original instructions at home instead of relying on memory. Teachers may also give written comments alongside an assignment, so that pupils can refer to them when revising. Used in this way, a platform supports learning rather than merely replacing paper with a screen.

Nevertheless, access is not equal in every household. A family may have a shared device or an unreliable connection, making an online deadline difficult to meet. Schools should therefore provide access to computers on site and allow an alternative submission method when necessary. They should also avoid assuming that an automatic mark explains an error: pupils still need opportunities to ask questions and discuss their work with a teacher.

In conclusion, schools use these platforms because they simplify the distribution and collection of homework. Their use is a positive development provided that access is addressed and technology remains a means of supporting, rather than replacing, teaching.
